options.metric: Annual count of reported cyclist deaths and annual count of reported motorist deaths, calculated by summing the corresponding per-crash fields
options.denominator: None; these are counts, not rates
options.grouping: Calendar year and victim group (cyclist, motorist)
options.reason: A direct comparison of annual counts preserves the magnitude of deaths in each victim group and their trends over time.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year, ranging from 72–139 motorist deaths versus 10–31 cyclist deaths annually; motorist deaths peaked at 139 in 2020, while cyclist deaths peaked at 31 in 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the year-by-year comparison in absolute numbers: motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year, with annual counts of 72–139 for motorists and 10–31 for cyclists. A two-series annual line chart is defensible because it preserves the actual count scale and shows both groups over the same calendar years. It does not adjust for the number of travelers or distance traveled, so it cannot compare individual risk; 2,132,218 crash rows are included and every year from 2013 through 2025 has a full-year date span. Neither death field has any NULL or negative values; 2,131,942 cyclist-field values (99.99%) and 2,130,945 motorist-field values (99.94%) are zero, and we kept these as valid no-death counts rather than dropping them; full-year date spans do not establish reporting completeness.

options.metric: Annual net difference in reported deaths (motorist deaths minus cyclist deaths), calculated from the corresponding per-crash fields
options.denominator: None; this is a difference in counts, not a rate
options.chart_type: Annual bar chart of the motorist-minus-cyclist difference
options.reason: The annual gap makes the size and direction of the count difference especially easy to compare across years.
options.answer: The motorist-minus-cyclist death gap was positive every year, ranging from 51 deaths in 2019 to 115 in 2021, and was 58 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how large the annual count difference is: motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths each year, by 51–115 deaths, with the largest gap in 2021 and the smallest in 2019. A bar chart of motorist deaths minus cyclist deaths is defensible because zero marks equality and bar height directly represents the annual gap. It leaves out each group's separate count and does not adjust for traveler numbers or distance traveled, so it cannot compare individual risk; the population is 2,132,218 crash rows with a full-year date span in every year from 2013 through 2025. Neither death field has any NULL or negative values; 2,131,942 cyclist-field values (99.99%) and 2,130,945 motorist-field values (99.94%) are zero, and we retained them as valid no-death counts; the full-year date spans do not establish reporting completeness.
